own_solution.law: Circular-orbit energy is E = -GMm/(2r), with GM = g0 Re². Therefore W = (m g0 Re²/2)[1/(Re+h1) - 1/(Re+h2)].
assumptions: The stated inverse-square gravitational field is fixed.
The initial and final orbits are circular.
Engine work supplies the change in orbital mechanical energy.
Additional instruments carried by the satellite remain aboard throughout the transfer.

notes: All certified answers agree with the orbital-energy calculation: additional satellite loads of 45, 95 and 170 kg give approximately 2777910, 2933100 and 3165890 kJ, respectively; every disconnected addition preserves 2638240 kJ. Using lengths numerically in km and g0 in m/s² makes the displayed relation return kJ, since kg·m·km/s² equals kJ. The pass-1 answers expressed in J agree after conversion. I withdraw the pass-1 high rendering flag: pass 2 identifies T1748 and TB6C9 explicitly as numeral-free controls, rather than claiming they retain the numerical value of their twins. Both expressly claimed minimal pairs retain 95 kg and change the intended attachment or event.
